set_title: Acro- names: things at the ends of the body (hands, feet, face)
stem: A 60-year-old Black man has had a dark streak under his right great toenail for 8 months. The pigment now extends onto the nail fold. Biopsy shows atypical pigmented cells spreading along the basal layer.
oneliner: 60-year-old Black man, 8-month dark toenail streak + pigment onto nail fold + atypical basal pigmented cells → ?

whyNot.A: Acromegaly enlarges hands and feet but does not cause **a pigmented nail streak**
whyNot.C: Acrodermatitis enteropathica is an infant zinc-deficiency rash; he has an **8-month pigmented nail streak**
whyNot.D: Acrocyanosis is a transient newborn color change; his streak is **dark, spreading and biopsy-proven**
whyNot.E: Acrochordon is a benign skin tag; his lesion shows **atypical pigmented cells on biopsy**

why: Acral (extremity) + lentiginous (spreading along the basal layer) + melanoma. **A dark nail streak with nail-fold pigment in a darker-skinned patient**; not sun-related.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **High IGF-1; GH not suppressed by glucose**

idea.rule: Acral lentiginous melanoma: palms, soles, nails; the commonest melanoma in dark skin.
also: Hutchinson sign: pigment on nail fold

set_title: Paget names: bone remodeling vs breast and skin cancer (and an effort clot)
stem: A 72-year-old woman has had an itchy, red, weeping plaque on the vulva for a year. Biopsy shows large pale cells containing mucin in the epidermis that stain PAS-positive. Breast examination and mammography are normal.
oneliner: 72-year-old woman, 1-year itchy red weeping vulvar plaque + large PAS-positive cells in epidermis + normal breasts → ?

whyNot.A: Paget disease of bone is skeletal; she has a **vulvar plaque with PAS-positive cells**
whyNot.B: Paget disease of the breast involves the nipple; her **breasts are normal**
whyNot.C: Paget-Schroetter is an arm vein thrombosis; she has a **vulvar plaque**
whyNot.E: Page kidney is a hypertension syndrome; she has a **vulvar plaque with PAS-positive cells**

why: Intraepithelial adenocarcinoma of apocrine skin sites (vulva, perianal). **A weeping vulvar plaque with PAS-positive cells and normal breasts**; look for a hidden internal cancer.

idea.rule: Extramammary Paget: same cells as breast Paget, but vulva or anus.
also: Screen for underlying GI or GU cancer

set_title: Skin lesion words: flat vs raised, small vs large, fluid vs solid
stem: A 70-year-old woman has tense, clear fluid-filled blisters 2 cm across on her flexures and thighs. The blisters do not rupture when pressed. The lesions are very itchy.
oneliner: 70-year-old woman, tense clear fluid-filled blisters 2 cm across on flexures + itchy → ?

whyNot.A: A vesicle is a blister under 1 cm; her blisters are **2 cm across**
whyNot.B: A plaque is a raised solid lesion over 1 cm; hers are **fluid-filled**
whyNot.C: A papule is a small solid bump; hers are **fluid-filled and 2 cm**
whyNot.D: A macule is flat and cannot be felt; hers are **raised, tense and fluid-filled**

why: Latin for bubble: a fluid-filled blister over 1 cm. **Tense clear 2-cm blisters** in an older woman fit bullae, as in bullous pemphigoid.

idea.rule: Size cut-off is 1 cm: vesicle under, bulla over; macule under, patch over.

set_title: Skin lesion words: flat vs raised, small vs large, fluid vs solid
stem: A 25-year-old man has raised, red, solid lesions with silvery scale, 3 cm across, on both elbows and knees. They are not fluid-filled and are palpable.
oneliner: 25-year-old man, raised red solid lesions 3 cm with silvery scale on elbows and knees → ?

whyNot.A: A macule is flat; his lesions are **raised and palpable**
whyNot.B: A patch is flat and over 1 cm; his lesions are **raised and solid**
whyNot.D: A papule is raised and solid under 1 cm; his are **3 cm across**
whyNot.E: A vesicle is a small fluid-filled blister; his lesions are **solid and 3 cm**

why: Plaque = raised flat-topped plate over 1 cm, solid. **Raised, silvery-scaled solid lesions 3 cm across** are the plaques of psoriasis.

idea.rule: Plaque is a raised lesion over 1 cm; patch is flat over 1 cm.

set_title: Skin lesion words: flat vs raised, small vs large, fluid vs solid
stem: An 8-year-old boy with neurofibromatosis type 1 has several light-brown spots on his trunk, each 5 mm across. The spots are flat and cannot be felt on running a finger across them.
oneliner: 8-year-old boy, NF1 + several flat light-brown spots 5 mm across, not palpable → ?

whyNot.A: A patch is flat but over 1 cm; his spots are **5 mm across**
whyNot.B: A papule is raised and palpable; his spots are **flat and cannot be felt**
whyNot.C: A plaque is raised, over 1 cm; his spots are **flat and 5 mm**
whyNot.E: A vesicle is a raised blister; his spots are **flat and solid in color**

why: Macule = flat color change under 1 cm; the one-centimeter rule separates it from a patch. **Flat, non-palpable 5-mm light-brown spots** are café-au-lait macules.

idea.rule: Flat and small is a macule; flat and big is a patch.

set_title: Erythema names: six red rashes with very different causes
stem: A 21-year-old woman had a cold sore 10 days ago and now has target lesions with three color zones on her palms and the backs of her hands. Mucous membranes are spared and she is not ill.
oneliner: 21-year-old woman, cold sore 10 days ago + three-zone target lesions on palms + mucosa spared → ?

whyNot.B: Erythema migrans is one large expanding ring; she has **many small palm target lesions**
whyNot.C: Erythema nodosum is tender shin nodules; she has **target lesions on her palms**
whyNot.D: Erythema marginatum has evanescent trunk rings; she has **fixed target lesions on palms**
whyNot.E: Erythema infectiosum causes red cheeks and lacy rash; she has **palm target lesions**

why: Multiforme = many shapes: a hypersensitivity rash with target lesions, often after HSV. **Three-zone targets on the palms after a cold sore** with spared mucosa.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Evanescent pink rings on trunk; rheumatic fever**
**Slapped cheeks, then lacy limb rash; parvovirus**

idea.rule: Multiforme: target lesions after HSV; severe mucosal loss means SJS.

set_title: Kerat-/acanth- skin names: actinic vs seborrheic keratosis, keratoacanthoma, acanthosis
stem: A 70-year-old farmer has several rough, scaly, skin-colored patches on his forehead and scalp that feel like sandpaper. They do not bleed or ulcerate and have grown slowly over 5 years. He has fair skin and many years of sun exposure.
oneliner: 70M, farmer, fair skin + sandpaper-rough scaly patches on forehead and scalp → ?

options.B: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

whyNot.A: Seborrheic keratosis is a waxy stuck-on plaque; his patches are **rough, scaly and sun-exposed**
whyNot.B: Squamous cell carcinoma is ulcerated; his patches **do not bleed or ulcerate**
whyNot.C: Acanthosis nigricans is velvety fold skin; his patches are **scaly on the forehead**
whyNot.D: Keratoacanthoma grows fast with a central crater; his lesions **grew slowly over 5 years**

why: Actin = ray (sun). Sun damage gives keratin overgrowth: **rough scaly patches on sun-exposed skin** can progress to squamous cell carcinoma.

idea.rule: Actinic keratosis = sun-damaged precancer; seborrheic = benign, stuck-on.
also: Treat with cryotherapy or topical fluorouracil

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Rough scaly sun-exposed papule; precancer to SCC**
Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

set_title: Kerat-/acanth- skin names: actinic vs seborrheic keratosis, keratoacanthoma, acanthosis
stem: A 65-year-old man has multiple waxy, brown, round plaques on his back that look stuck on. They have grown slowly over 10 years and are not painful. Close inspection shows tiny keratin-filled pits on the surface. The plaques are well-demarcated and the skin around them is normal.
oneliner: 65M, many waxy brown stuck-on plaques on back, slow growth, keratin pits → ?

options.E: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

whyNot.A: Acanthosis nigricans is velvety fold skin; his plaques are **waxy, on the back**
whyNot.B: Actinic keratosis is rough scaly sun-damaged skin; his plaques are **waxy and stuck on**
whyNot.D: Keratoacanthoma grows rapidly with a crater; his plaques **grew slowly over 10 years**
whyNot.E: Squamous cell carcinoma is ulcerated or crusted; his plaques are **waxy, stable and painless**

why: Seb = oily. A benign epidermal growth: **waxy stuck-on brown plaques with horn cysts** need no treatment.

idea.rule: Seborrheic keratosis = benign stuck-on plaque, horn cysts.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Rough scaly sun-exposed papule; precancer to SCC**
Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

set_title: Kerat-/acanth- skin names: actinic vs seborrheic keratosis, keratoacanthoma, acanthosis
stem: A 60-year-old man has a dome-shaped, 2-cm nodule on his cheek that appeared 6 weeks ago and has grown quickly. The center is filled with a keratin plug that forms a crater. The nodule is flesh-colored with a smooth edge and is not painful.
oneliner: 60M, dome nodule on cheek, 6 weeks, central keratin plug crater → ?

options.E: Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

whyNot.B: Seborrheic keratosis is a slow waxy plaque; his lesion **appeared 6 weeks ago**
whyNot.C: Acanthosis nigricans is velvety dark skin; his lesion is **a fast dome nodule**
whyNot.D: Actinic keratosis is flat and scaly; his lesion is **a crater-forming nodule**
whyNot.E: Squamous cell carcinoma grows over months; his grew **within 6 weeks as a crater**

why: Kerato = keratin, acanth = spiny layer. A low-grade squamous growth: **fast dome nodule with a keratin crater** that often regresses.

idea.rule: Keratoacanthoma = fast dome with crater; regresses but resembles SCC.
also: Biopsy to separate from squamous carcinoma

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Rough scaly sun-exposed papule; precancer to SCC**
Squamous cell carcinoma of the skin

set_title: Hemangio- names: infantile, cherry, cavernous, hemangioblastoma, pyogenic granuloma
stem: A 2-month-old girl has a bright red, raised, soft lesion on her cheek. It was a faint red spot at birth and has tripled in size over 6 weeks. She is otherwise healthy and feeding well. Her mother asks what to expect.
oneliner: 2-month-old girl, bright red raised cheek lesion, tiny at birth then fast growth → ?

whyNot.A: Cherry hemangioma is a small adult papule; hers is **a growing infant lesion**
whyNot.B: Pyogenic granuloma bleeds after trauma; hers is **a soft growing infant mark**
whyNot.C: Cavernous hemangioma is a deep tumor; hers is **a bright red surface lesion**
whyNot.E: Bacillary angiomatosis occurs in AIDS; she is **a healthy 2-month-old**

why: Infantile = baby. A capillary tumor that **grows in months then regresses by childhood**, rarely needing treatment.

idea.rule: Infantile hemangioma = grows then regresses; propranolol if it threatens function.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Most common benign liver tumor; don't biopsy**
**Red papules in AIDS; neutrophils on biopsy**

set_title: Hemangio- names: infantile, cherry, cavernous, hemangioblastoma, pyogenic granuloma
stem: A 28-year-old woman at 20 weeks of pregnancy has a red, 1-cm, dome-shaped nodule on her gum. It appeared 3 weeks ago, bleeds with brushing, and is friable with a collarette of skin at its base. It is painless and she has no fever.
oneliner: 28F, 20 weeks pregnant, red friable gum nodule bleeding after brushing → ?

whyNot.B: Cherry hemangioma is a small stable papule; hers **grew over 3 weeks and bleeds**
whyNot.C: Infantile hemangioma appears in infants; she is **a pregnant adult**
whyNot.D: Hemangioblastoma is a brain tumor; hers is **a gum nodule**
whyNot.E: Bacillary angiomatosis occurs in AIDS; she has **pregnancy and a single gum nodule**

why: A misnomer: there is neither pus nor granuloma, but capillary overgrowth. **A friable bleeding papule in pregnancy or after trauma** is typical.

idea.rule: Pyogenic granuloma = misnamed: capillary growth that bleeds in pregnancy.

head: Term
Means
One clue
rows: **Most common benign liver tumor; don't biopsy**
**Red papules in AIDS; neutrophils on biopsy**

set_title: Genital lesion names: chancre, chancroid, condyloma lata, condylomata acuminata, granuloma inguinale, LGV
stem: A 22-year-old woman has soft, flesh-colored, verrucous growths on the vulva and perianal area for 2 months. They are painless and itch slightly. Application of 5% acetic acid whitens them. Biopsy shows squamous cells with perinuclear halos and wrinkled nuclei.
oneliner: 22F, soft cauliflower-like growths on vulva and perineum, koilocytes on biopsy → ?

whyNot.A: Chancroid is a painful ulcer; hers are **warty growths with koilocytes**
whyNot.B: Condylomata lata are flat, gray and moist with syphilis; hers are **pointed and cauliflower-like**
whyNot.D: Granuloma inguinale is a beefy red ulcer; hers are **warty growths**
whyNot.E: Lymphogranuloma venereum has buboes; hers are **warts with koilocytes**

why: Acuminate = pointed. HPV types 6 and 11 cause **pointed cauliflower warts with koilocytes**, unlike the flat plaques of secondary syphilis.

idea.rule: Acuminata = pointed HPV warts; lata = broad flat syphilis plaques.
